title: Send a server-initiated message to the terminal it is meant for

blocks.text: Before a store closes for the night, the server signs its terminals off: an `0800` with field 70 = `002`, addressed to one terminal through field 41. A batch job builds these messages and calls `TerminalDirectory.send` for each. Today half of the sign-offs arrive at the wrong till, and the till they were meant for keeps transacting.
`TerminalDirectory` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TerminalDirectory.java` is a request listener that goes first in the QServer's chain. Finish its two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `process(source, m)`: called for every message the server receives;
`send(m)`: sends `m` to its terminal, and returns `false` when that terminal can't be reached now (the batch job retries those later).

blocks.text: Terminals reconnect during the day, and some are switched off without closing anything. About eight lines in total.
The tests play QServer: they offer each message to the directory and then to a stand-in for the rest of the chain, and their connections can be closed.

cases.says: after a terminal has sent a message, a message addressed to it through field 41 is sent on its connection
the directory returns false, so every request still reaches the listeners that answer it
a terminal that reconnected is reached on its newest connection
a terminal whose connection is closed, or that never connected, is reported as not reached, without a send
with two terminals connected, a message goes to the one it is addressed to, not to the one that connected last
a message without field 41 passes through the directory without an error

origin.section: 3.5 The Server Picks the Connection for a Message It Starts

concepts: A message the server starts goes to the connection the server chooses: QServer's in queue sends to the last connection, so a terminal is addressed through the source it last used, kept per terminal ID.
